title: The Warranty (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word cabaret 102bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan male vocal absurdist dry comedy warm vinyl
lyrics:
[Intro - dry piano, careful pace]
I want to tell you about a man
Who kept all his warranties
In a filing cabinet
In the spare room

[Verse 1]
Every appliance, every device
Every piece of furniture with a guarantee
He read the documentation thoroughly
And filed it alphabetically

The toaster is under T
The refrigerator under R
The television under T as well
But behind the toaster, chronologically

He had a system, and the system was sound
Seventeen years of documentation, neatly bound
No warranty had ever been needed
Because he had all the warranties

[Pre-Chorus]
And then one morning, without warning
Something in the spare room made a sound
He went to look and the filing cabinet
Was lying quietly on the ground

[Chorus]
Everything was covered except the filing cabinet
The filing cabinet had no warranty
Everything was covered except the filing cabinet
It had not come with documentation
He stood there in the spare room
For a considerable amount of time
Everything was covered except the filing cabinet
The filing cabinet was not covered

[Verse 2]
He called the manufacturer on a Tuesday
They said the model was discontinued in 2011
He said the model had been discontinued in 2011
They said yes that's what we said

[Bridge - spoken, quite still]
He considered his options
He had several
The strongest was irony
He did not file it

[Chorus]
Everything was covered except the filing cabinet
The filing cabinet had no warranty
Everything was covered except the filing cabinet
It had not come with documentation
He stood there in the spare room
For a considerable amount of time
Everything was covered except the filing cabinet
The filing cabinet was not covered

[Outro - piano notes, widely spaced]
He bought a new filing cabinet
He did not keep the warranty
He felt this was the right call
He filed this feeling under W
